court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
case_name: M/S Dwarka Prasad Agrawal & Brothers vs Registrar, Firms, Societies & Chits & 3

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: M/s Dwarika Prasad Agarwal & Brothers and another (Petitioners)
parties.respondent_defendant: Registrar, Firms, Societies and Chits, U.P. and others (Opp. parties)

facts_of_case: Firm constituted in 1972; registered with Assistant Registrar, Firms, Societies and Chits, Jhansi on 15.11.1976. Partners running separate businesses regarding publication of newspaper from different cities.

legal_principles.principle: A party invoking the High Court's jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution is duty bound to place all facts before the court without any reservation.
legal_principles.held: The apex Court held that in exercising power under Article 226 of the Constitution, the High Court is not just a court of law, but is also a court of equity and a person who invokes the High Court's jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution is duty bound to place all the facts before the court without any reservation.
cited_cases: Prestige Lights Ltd. v. State Bank of India, (2007) 8 SCC 449
R v. Kensington Income Tax Commissioners
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to deter unscrupulous litigants from abusing the process of Court by deceiving it

legal_principles.principle: A party which has misled the Court in passing an order in its favour is not entitled to be heard on the merits of the case.
legal_principles.held: The apex Court held that a party which has misled the Court in passing an order in its favour is not entitled to be heard on the merits of the case.
cited_cases: Welcome Hotel and Ors. v. State of Andhra Pradesh and Ors.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to ensure that parties do not take advantage of the Court's process
